Katherine: Quick question — can managers submit out-of-cycle comp increases for retention? We have someone asking and I want to confirm process and timing.

Jamal (People Ops): Short answer: yes, but there are a few constraints.

Katherine: Constraints = approvals? effective date? budget owner?

Jamal (People Ops): All of the above. High level: 1) Manager submits the comp-change request form, 2) Comp team reviews for band/benchmarks, 3) Finance signs off for budget, 4) People Ops finalizes paperwork & payroll timeline.

Katherine: Where's the form? any template?

comp-ops-bot: Form link: <https://redwood.internal/hr/comp-change-format> — please fill all fields. CSV upload supported for batch requests.

Ben (Eng Manager): If it's for retention (counteroffers), can we backdate to the original request month?

Priya (Comp): We try not to backdate. Effective dates must align with payroll cutoffs. For monthly payroll, changes submitted by the 10th of the month can be effective on the 1st of next month; submissions after that usually go into the following cycle. Exceptions need Finance approval.

Katherine: Is there a separate approval path for equity adjustments vs base salary?

Priya (Comp): Yes — equity adjustments need Comp + Legal review (for plan limits) and then Finance. Base salary increases go through Comp + Finance only. Stock refreshes and RSU grants have an additional compensation committee cadence — those can't be ad-hoc.

Ben (Eng Manager): What's the minimum info we should include to speed approval?

Jamal (People Ops): Put these in the form: employee name, current comp (base + bonus + eq), proposed comp, reason (retention/market/lateral promo), manager justification (1-2 bullets), and any supporting offer data. If you have a competing offer, attach redacted docs.

Katherine: How long does review take?

Priya (Comp): Typical turnaround 3–5 business days for straightforward requests. If Finance questions budget or it requires comp committee, add ~2 weeks.

Katherine: If comp is denied, is there an appeal or escalation?

Jamal (People Ops): Managers can request a re-review with additional justification or propose alternative levers (one-time bonus, title change, stretch role). For escalations, ping @Priya and me; include the approval ticket ID from the form.

Ben (Eng Manager): Any required CCs on the form? I assume People Ops and Finance?

comp-ops-bot: Required reviewers: comp-team@redwood, finance-approvals@redwood. Optional: hr-business-partner.

Katherine: Are there compensation band limits (i.e., we can't exceed band max without exec approval)?

Priya (Comp): Correct — anything above band max requires VP People + Finance sign-off and sometimes CEO depending on % over. We document exceptions in the approval notes.

Ben (Eng Manager): Is there guidance for managers about communication to employee on denial/partial approval?

Jamal (People Ops): Yes — short script in the manager playbook. Key points: be transparent about the decision rationale, offer timeline for re-evaluation, and discuss alternative retention tools (bonus, career path). Link: <https://redwood.internal/hr/manager-playbook#comp-changes>

Katherine: One last — mid-cycle promotions that include base changes: do we route them through the same flow?

Priya (Comp): Promotions that change comp go through the comp-change form but add the promo justification and new job family/band fields. If it's a promotion without comp change, mark as "title-only" and notify HR for title update only.

Katherine: thanks — super helpful. I'll submit the form and attach the redacted offer. :thumbsup:

Ben (Eng Manager): Thanks everyone — saving this thread for my managers.

Jamal (People Ops): If anyone wants a quick sync, drop a time and I'll set up a 15-min slot.

comp-ops-bot: Reminder: batch CSV template is available here: <https://redwood.internal/hr/comp-batch-template.csv>. CSV columns: employee_id,current_base,current_bonus,current_eq,proposed_base,proposed_bonus,reason,manager_notes.

Katherine: scheduling a quick sync for tomorrow 10am.

Priya (Comp): I'll join.

Ben (Eng Manager): I'll be there too.

Jamal (People Ops): Great — see you all.
